name: cobalt
label: Shesha Cobalt (Ant Design stock + one brand override)

provenance.source: Externally supplied Shesha design-system handover: design-system.md and shesha-theme.ts. Values transcribed, not chosen.
provenance.note: Offered as a THIRD theme, not as the default. The house design system is the LandBank kit (#0d685a) and the reference app's live theme is currently #2197dc; three different primaries cannot all be the default, and picking between them is a brand decision rather than a generator's.
provenance.whyItIsStillWorthHaving: It is the strongest test of the token boundary in the set. Where LandBank and WCG share one anatomy under two brands, Cobalt comes from a different design lineage entirely — stock Ant Design with a single seed override, a 4px spacing grid, 6px control radius and Ant's own semantic colours. If switching to it changes anything STRUCTURAL, the boundary leaks.
provenance.versionCaveat: The handover targets Ant Design v6.3.5, but the reference app has antd 5.27.6 installed. Only the values that are brand decisions rather than antd-major-specific derivations are transcribed here. The v6 per-component token dictionary was deliberately NOT carried over, because it describes a package this app does not have.

inkNote: Derived by Ant from the colorTextBase seed #181818 (Shesha Nero). The quaternary ramp value rgba(24,24,24,0.25) is deliberately NOT used as inkFaint: it measures 1.73:1 on white and fails WCAG AA, so the tertiary value carries that role instead.
semanticNote: sage, purple, accentBlue and accentTeal are ALL null — this lineage has no decorative accent roles at all, only Ant's four semantic colours. That makes Cobalt the strictest test of nullable-role handling: a consumer that substitutes its own colour for a null role will be visibly wrong here.

type.fontFamily: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, 'Noto Sans', sans-serif
type.fontMono: SFMono-Regular, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', Menlo, Courier, monospace
type.microLabelNote: 12px, not 11px. This lineage floors readable type at 14px and reserves 12px for help text, timestamps, metadata and tags — so its micro-label is one notch larger than the LandBank kit's measured 11px.
type.trackingNote: Zero tracking throughout. This lineage does not use letter-spacing as a design device, where the house kit uses .04em on 116 elements.

microLabel.note: Sentence case, not uppercase, and no tracking. The uppercase micro-label is a LandBank/WCG device, not an Ant one.

spacing.note: A genuinely strict 4px grid, unlike LandBank's measured 2px grid and WCG's odd-biased one. This is the theme where a 'multiples of 4' rule would actually hold — which is exactly why that rule must live in the token file rather than in a validator.

elevation.shadowCardNote: Flat by default; a 1px border does the work. Same philosophy as the house kit, reached independently.

statusModelNote: Ant tags are a tinted background with a semantic border and dark text, so this lineage is tint rather than solid.
referenceListRampNote: Empty deliberately. This lineage has no lifecycle colour ramp — status colour comes from Ant's four semantic colours only. Seeding a Shesha reference list under this theme means choosing among those four, not painting a 16-value ramp.

accessibility.note: The one thing this handover contributes that neither the build brief nor the house design standard covers: measured WCAG 2.2 AA failures in Ant's own defaults. Carried here as data so the Phase 6 rendered gates can compute contrast from the DOM rather than assert it.

antDefaultsFailingAA.role: fails as text and as fill
amber cannot carry white text at any usable saturation
